**Observations:**

- W1 has a sharp two‑regime structure. About 67–70 pixels sit exactly in the PyTorch default init range (uniform ±1/√784 ≈ ±0.036) with no sign of training: all of row 0 except columns 12–15 (inputs 0–11, 16–27), row 1 cols 0–3 and 24–27, row 2 cols 0–1 and 26–27, row 3 cols 0–1 and 27, col 0 at rows 4–6/17/20/23–27, col 1 at rows 5/23–25, col 27 at rows 23–25, row 26 cols 0–3/26–27, row 27 cols 0–3/24–27. That set (including the tiny weakly‑trained patch at row 0 cols 12–15, and faint weights at rare edge pixels like (4,27), (7,0), (14–16,0), (21,0), (26,24–25), (27,4)) is essentially MNIST's always‑zero/near‑zero pixel set. Everything else is clearly trained. No trained-looking weights appear in any corner or dead region, so there is no trigger patch in the "free" input space.
- Within the trained region, every hidden unit's weight map is spatially smooth (neighbouring pixels have correlated values, no isolated hot pixels), and all 16 units have broad, distinct, stroke‑like patterns; no dead, duplicate, or sparse unit. Largest magnitudes (~0.5–0.6) are at the periphery — rows 1–3 (units 7, 14, 4, 2 negative), rows 25–27 (units 2, 5 positive; 14, 15 negative), and cols 24–25 rows 7–11 (unit 8, 2, 4 ≈ −0.5). Those peripheral sign patterns line up with the W2 columns for classes 6 (top ink), 9/7 (bottom ink) and 5 (right‑edge ink), i.e. the network has learned the centre‑of‑mass shift cues of MNIST; this is what Adam‑style training without weight decay does on rarely‑active but class‑informative pixels.
- b1 moderate (|b| ≤ 0.42). W2 entries all |w| ≤ 1.11, mixed signs, every row and column of comparable norm, no dominant unit→class weight, no exact zeros or repeated values. b2 small (−0.43…0.37).

**Unusual:** No

**What:** nothing

**Confidence:** 20%
